packages.name: queue
packages.doc:
Package queue is a core/data/queue Broker over a NATS JetStream stream and
one durable pull consumer (ADR 0054's deferred connector, ADR 0211), in the
third-party/nats vendor module.

# Mapping

Publish is a JetStream publication the stream acknowledges (PubAck); the
stream sequence is the message's ID, and the enqueue instant, read from
Config.Clock, travels in a header. Receive is a Fetch of up to max
messages that waits for none; the delivery count is the server's
NumDelivered. Ack is an acknowledgement the server confirms (a double
acknowledgement); Nack is a NakWithDelay by the retry delay, or, once the
message has been delivered MaxDeliveries times, a publication on the
dead-letter subject with its cause followed by Term — two requests, so a
crash between them dead-letters the message twice and never loses it. The
consumer has no MaxDeliver of its own: the broker owns the decision to
dead-letter (ADR 0054), and a message whose leases all lapsed is
dead-lettered by the Receive that finds it past its budget, its Reason
LEASE_EXPIRED. Kafka is not this port — it has no per-message
acknowledgement — and belongs to data/stream.

# Whose clock is the lease

The server redelivers on its own clock once AckWait passes. The broker
reads Config.Clock before each Fetch, so the deadline it hands out never
falls after the server's, and the lease is the policy's visibility timeout
or the consumer's AckWait, whichever is shorter. It refuses an Ack, Nack,
Extend or Reject at or past that deadline with
core/data/queue.LeaseExpired before anything is sent, so a consumer that
lost its lease learns it whatever the server did meanwhile. A receipt is
good with the broker that issued it, whose table holds the delivery that
acknowledges it; one another broker minted is
core/data/queue.UnknownReceipt.

# The stream

Config.CreateStream creates a work-queue stream over Subject and
DeadLetterSubject, so an acknowledged message leaves it and a dead letter,
which no consumer reads, stays; and the durable consumer, filtered on
Subject, its AckWait the policy's visibility timeout. A stream made by
hand must capture both subjects too: DeadLetters reads the dead-letter
subject back from the same stream by direct get, without consuming it.

# Capabilities

Waker (a publication or hand-back by this process, and the next deadline
it knows of), LeaseExtender (InProgress resets AckWait, so a renewal lasts
the shorter of the asked duration and AckWait), Rejecter, DelayedNacker
(NakWithDelay), OncePublisher (Nats-Msg-Id; JetStream deduplicates over
the stream's duplicate window and no other, so the window asked for must
be that one) and DeadLetterReader. Not Releaser: the server's delivery
count cannot be given back. Every failed request is the package's
sentinel, core/data/queue.QueueBackendFailed in its trail.

symbols.name: CodeJetStreamConsumerMissing
symbols.doc: CodeJetStreamConsumerMissing identifies a durable consumer the stream does not have.

symbols.name: CodeJetStreamMisconfigured
symbols.doc:
CodeJetStreamMisconfigured identifies a Config NewJetStream refuses
before any request: no connection, an empty stream, subject or consumer
name, a policy JetStream cannot honour.

symbols.name: CodeJetStreamPublishUnacked
symbols.doc:
CodeJetStreamPublishUnacked identifies a publication the stream did not
acknowledge: it may or may not be stored.

symbols.name: CodeJetStreamRequestFailed
symbols.doc: CodeJetStreamRequestFailed identifies any other JetStream failure, the cause kept in the chain.

symbols.name: CodeJetStreamServerUnreachable
symbols.doc: CodeJetStreamServerUnreachable identifies a connection that is closed or a request that timed out.

symbols.name: CodeJetStreamStreamMissing
symbols.doc:
CodeJetStreamStreamMissing identifies a stream the server does not have
while Config.CreateStream is false.

symbols.name: Config
symbols.spelled: struct{Conn *nats.Conn; Clock clock.Clock; Stream string; Subject string; DeadLetterSubject string; Consumer string; Policy corequeue.PolicyValue; Timeout time.Duration; CreateStream bool}

fields.name: Conn
fields.doc: Conn is the caller's connection; the broker never closes it. Required.

fields.name: Clock
fields.doc:
Clock stamps the enqueue instant and the lease deadlines a receipt
carries, and judges them. Nil means clock.System.

fields.name: Stream
fields.doc: Stream names the JetStream stream that holds the queue. Required.

fields.name: Subject
fields.doc:
Subject is the subject messages are published on; the stream must
capture it. Required.

fields.name: DeadLetterSubject
fields.doc:
DeadLetterSubject is the subject a message is published on, with its
cause, once it is dead-lettered; the stream must capture it too, and
the consumer never reads it. Required.

fields.name: Consumer
fields.doc: Consumer is the durable pull consumer every broker of the queue shares. Required.

fields.name: Policy
fields.doc:
Policy is the delivery discipline: VisibilityTimeout is AckWait. Its
zero value is refused, as for every broker.

fields.name: Timeout
fields.doc:
Timeout bounds every request that waits on the server — a publication's
PubAck, an acknowledgement's confirmation. Zero is refused (ADR 0031).

fields.name: CreateStream
fields.doc:
CreateStream creates the stream, over Subject and DeadLetterSubject,
and the consumer, when first use finds them missing. False answers
StreamMissing or ConsumerMissing instead.

symbols.doc:
Config configures NewJetStream: the connection, the stream, its subject and
dead-letter subject, the durable consumer, and the delivery discipline.

symbols.name: ConsumerMissing

code.public: The queue's consumer does not exist

symbols.doc: ConsumerMissing reports a durable consumer the stream does not have.

symbols.name: DefaultDuplicateWindow
symbols.doc:
DefaultDuplicateWindow is the duplicate window of a stream
Config.CreateStream creates — JetStream's own default — and so the one
window PublishOnce accepts on such a stream.

symbols.name: JetStreamMisconfigured

code.public: The JetStream queue broker is misconfigured

symbols.doc: JetStreamMisconfigured refuses a Config NewJetStream cannot build a broker from.

symbols.name: NewJetStream
symbols.doc:
NewJetStream returns a broker over cfg.Stream and its durable consumer
cfg.Consumer. It sends no request: the stream and the consumer are looked
up, or created when cfg.CreateStream asks, on first use. A policy the
broker cannot honour is core/data/queue.QueueMisconfigured; a missing
connection or name is JetStreamMisconfigured.

symbols.name: PublishUnacked

code.public: The queue did not confirm the message

symbols.doc: PublishUnacked reports a publication the stream did not acknowledge.

symbols.name: RequestFailed
symbols.doc: RequestFailed wraps any other JetStream failure.

symbols.name: ServerUnreachable

code.public: The queue server could not be reached

symbols.doc: ServerUnreachable wraps a closed connection or a timed-out request.

symbols.name: StreamMissing

code.public: The queue's stream does not exist

symbols.doc: StreamMissing reports a stream the server does not have.
